item.description: An edge gains tail, end labels with boxes, curve, and line; head takes the full terminator vocabulary. The schema and validation name every bad value.
item.label: Connector fields on an edge

item.description: Arrows, UML ends, and ERD crow's feet drawn in a 10x10 box; a tail faces outward via auto-start-reverse, and hollow parts fill with the canvas.
item.label: One terminator vocabulary

item.body: You might expect head size to stay fixed; without head_size, a terminator now grows with strokes thicker than 2. No published diagram has one, so none re-render.
item.description: Why a thick arrow's head changes size.
item.label: Thick arrows grow

item.description: curve smooth draws a Catmull-Rom curve through the points; line overrides the style's dash with dashed or round-capped dots.
item.label: Smooth, dashed, or dotted

item.description: head_label and tail_label draw short text such as 1 or N at an edge's ends, each in its own explicit box.
item.label: End labels

item.description: The edge renderer now asks connectors.go for its path, dash, markers, and end labels; everything without the new fields renders exactly as before.
item.label: The renderer dispatches

item.description: describe adds tail=, head=, and end labels when they say more than a plain arrow, in text and JSON.
item.label: describe prints cardinality

slide.takeaway: An edge now has a head and a tail from one vocabulary of arrows, UML ends, and ERD crow's feet, plus end labels, smooth curves, and dashed or dotted lines.
slide.title: Edges end in terminators
